title: Coproducts of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $I$ be a set and let $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume there are surjective etale maps from schemes $U_i\to F_i$ whose scheme coproduct $\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] is an object of $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then the sheaf coproduct (the colimit of the discrete $I$-indexed diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) $F=\coprod_{i\in I}F_i$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is an algebraic space over $S$.

proof.text: By [def-trf-algebraic-space] the $F_i$ are fppf sheaves. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] to obtain their sheaf coproduct $F$, injective coprojections $c_i$, and the unique clopen partitions with component sections, compatible with restriction and with $h_{T_i(a)}\simeq h_T\times_FF_i$.

For $a,b\in F(T)$ put $D_i=T_i(a)\cap T_i(b)$. The representable diagonal of $F_i$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] gives a scheme $E_i$ representing equality of their component sections over $D_i$. Apply [lem-trf-coproduct-equality-locus]: $\coprod_iE_i$ represents $h_T\times_{F\times F}F$. This works for every $T$ and $(a,b)$, so the diagonal of $F$ is representable.

Let $U=\coprod_iU_i$ be the site object in the hypothesis. Its summands form a disjoint clopen covering [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The sections $c_i(p_i)\in F(U_i)$ agree on the empty overlaps: the empty-cover sheaf condition gives a unique section over the empty scheme. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] glues them to $p\in F(U)$, defining $p:h_U\to F$ by restriction along maps to $U$, with $p|_{U_i}=c_ip_i$.

source.place: Tag 02WQ (lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces), construction of the resulting atlas map

proof.text: For $a:h_T\to F$ and its partition $T_i$, the atlas conditions [def-trf-algebraic-space] give schemes $V_i=h_{T_i}\times_{F_i}h_{U_i}$ with surjective etale projections to $T_i$. Apply [lem-trf-coproduct-scheme-pullback] to $p$: $V=\coprod_iV_i$ represents $h_T\times_Fh_U$, and its projection restricts to $V_i\to T_i\to T$. Thus $p$ is representable.

source.place: Tag 02WQ (lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces), scheme-test verification of the atlas

proof.text: Every $t\in T$ lies in a unique $T_i$ and has a preimage in $V_i$, so $V\to T$ is surjective. At $v\in V_i$ choose affine etale charts for $V_i\to T_i$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. As $V_i\subset V$ and $T_i\subset T$ are open, they are the same affine charts and ring map for $V\to T$, which is therefore etale. For all $T\to F$ this proves the atlas is surjective etale. The three conditions of [def-trf-algebraic-space] now hold. If $I$ is empty the partition forces $T$ empty, and $U=V=\varnothing$; the checks are vacuous. Empty summands cause no change.

lean.statement: theorem algebraicSpace_coproduct {S : Scheme.{u}} (I : Type u) (F : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (U : I → Over S) (p : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (U i) ⟶ (F i).obj.obj) (hp : ∀ i, AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale (p i) ∧ AlgebraicSpace.IsSurjective (p i)) (Ucoprod : Over S) (ι : ∀ i, U i ⟶ Ucoprod) (hU : Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk Ucoprod ι))) (C : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (c : ∀ i, (F i).obj ⟶ C) (hC : IsColimit (Cofan.mk C c)) : AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace C

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches node/Stacks 02WQ clause by clause: S : Scheme.{u}; I : Type u (project set convention, as in the partition lemma at v=0); F : I → AlgebraicSpace S; atlases p i with representable IsEtale ∧ IsSurjective; size hypothesis as an IsColimit cofan in Over S (Over.forget creates colimits, so this is the scheme coproduct); conclusion IsAlgebraicSpace for every colimit cofan C (equivalent to 'the' coproduct, iso-invariant).
